facts.raw_span: a 2-week history of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules on his face, scalp, trunk, and extremities
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
prior treatment included prednisolone tablet 5 mg twice daily, clindamycin hydrochloride 300 mg daily, and fluconazole 200 mg daily
patient continued to develop new lesions
patient reported difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk along with keloidal plaques on the face
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing for HIV was negative
Punch biopsy from arm showed: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells
Negative periodic acid–Schiff staining

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration and microabscesses, is consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The patient's symptoms of fever, leukocytosis, and tender, erythematous skin lesions, along with the histopathological findings of dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, are consistent with Sweet Syndrome.

The patient's presentation of widespread, painful, and itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with the history of prior treatment and continued development of new lesions, is consistent with Eczema Herpeticum.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils, are consistent with Psoriasis.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with the histopathological findings of microabscesses and negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, is consistent with Dermatitis Herpetiformis.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with the histopathological findings of dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, are consistent with Seborrheic Dermatitis.
The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with the history of prior treatment and continued development of new lesions, is consistent with Impetigo.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with pustules and ulceration, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils, are consistent with Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with laboratory and histopathology results, including negative HIV testing and negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, are consistent with Acute Febrile Neutrophilic Dermatosis.
